import re

def predict(probe):
    # Model of the black box:
    # 1. Whitespace handling: the string is split into "words" on whitespace,
    #    where whitespace = any Unicode whitespace character (space, tab, newline,
    #    \v, \f, \r, NBSP \u00a0, em-space \u2003, thin-space \u2009, etc.).
    #    Leading/trailing whitespace is discarded; internal whitespace just separates.
    #    [E4, E6, E10, E12]
    # 2. The words are concatenated with no separator, then the whole result is
    #    reversed character-by-character (Unicode code points).
    #    [E1..E12 all consistent: e.g. "a b c" -> "cba", "Hello World" -> "dlroWolleH"]
    # 3. Empty input -> empty output (no words).
    # 4. Non-whitespace characters (letters, digits, punctuation, accents, CJK)
    #    are preserved and simply reversed. [E2, E8, E9]
    # 5. Case is preserved. [E1, E2, E8]

    def transform(s):
        # Split on any Unicode whitespace and drop empty pieces
        words = re.split(r'\s+', s, flags=re.UNICODE)
        words = [w for w in words if w != '']
        joined = ''.join(words)
        return joined[::-1]

    inputs = probe.get("inputs", [])
    outputs = []
    for s in inputs:
        try:
            outputs.append(transform(s))
        except Exception:
            outputs.append(s)
    return {"outputs": outputs}
notes: The box strips all whitespace (splitting on any Unicode whitespace and joining the pieces), then reverses the resulting string character-by-character.
